Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — a few clarifying Qs

Hi Evan —

Thanks for the product tour yesterday. Before I put together a formal sizing + pricing proposal for Dedicated, a couple quick clarifications on your request mix so we size the GPU pool and commit correctly:

- Current (expected) steady-state: ~120 QPS of text generation (API calls), with average payload ~550 tokens input + 150 tokens generation (total ~700 tokens/request).
- Peak launch day: observed spikes to ~420 QPS for short windows (~10–20 minutes).
- Context-length distribution: ~70% of requests are small (<=2k total tokens), ~25% are medium (2k–8k), ~5% are long (>8k, up to 32k).
- Concurrency: you called out wanting p99 latency guarantees under 400 concurrent users (sessions), but mentioned spikes to 1.2k concurrent during marketing campaigns.

Can you confirm those numbers (especially the long-context % and the maximum spike concurrency)? Also, do you expect many streaming responses or mostly single-shot generation?

If you prefer, I can draft two options: (A) conservative guarantee (sized for launch spike with higher commit, lower burst) and (B) lean guarantee (lower commit + larger burst buffer).

Attaching a short worksheet to fill if that helps.

Thanks —
Monica

- Steady-state: 150 QPS (we under-forecasted earlier) — median request ~850 tokens total (prompt + gen).
- Peak campaign spikes: up to 600 QPS sustained for 30–45 minutes (we saw that in last quarter's campaign).
- Context distribution: 60% small (<=2k), 30% medium (2k–12k), 10% long (12k–32k). Long-context requests are mostly fine-tuning inference and some long-form summarization.
- Concurrency: baseline concurrency ~350; peaks up to ~1,500 during spikes.
- Streaming vs single-shot: ~40% streaming (user-facing chat), 60% single-shot. Streaming tends to be lower tokens-per-call but higher sustained concurrency.

Budget: we're interested in a 12-month reserved commit if the economics make sense. Looking for a target effective discount in the 25–35% range versus on-demand hosted pricing.

Let me know if you want raw telemetry; we can share an S3 export.

Karthik / Ben —

Forwarding Velara's updated telemetry. They want a 12-mo commit and are targeting a 25–35% discount. Key constraints: steady 150 QPS, peaks 600 QPS sustained for ~30–45m, up to 1.5k concurrent. Long-context mix heavier than average (10% >12k). Streaming ~40%.

Initial thought from me: recommend a hybrid pool that guarantees steady throughput for the 90th percentile steady-state and provides a burst buffer for marketing spikes. Please review the arithmetic below and flag anything that looks off. If we land on numbers, I will send them a formal proposal and pricing sheet.

My quick calc (very rough):
- Target steady throughput: 150 QPS * 850 tokens/request = 127.5k tokens/sec (TPS)
- Effective tokens/sec required including medium/long requests and batching inefficiencies: +25% => ~160k TPS
- For long-context (10% of requests up to 32k) we should reserve extra memory (KV cache) and allow for lower batch efficiency.

Propose options:
A) Guarantee-heavy: 10 x L40S-equivalent cards (or 8 x A100-80GB equiv) sized to hit 160k TPS steady + 60% burst credits for campaign spikes. 12-mo commit with 25% discount.
B) Lean guarantee + burst pool: 6 x L40S-equivalent guarantee, plus a 4-card burst pool billed differently (burst credits or hourly). Lower commit, higher burst for campaigns.

Questions:
- Do we have modeled p95/p99 latencies for streaming vs single-shot at those pool sizes?
- What cache hit rate assumptions should we bake in for their usage?

Thanks —
Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Velara numbers — draft sizing ask (internal)

Monica —

Looks reasonable. A couple notes from runtime:

- Throughput assumptions: on L40S an optimized 7B-ish chat model at ~2k context can do roughly 18–22k tokens/sec per card with continuous batching; at 8k contexts that drops to ~9–12k TPS/card. For a mixed distribution like theirs, use a weighted average: expect ~14–16k TPS/card effective (we'll assume 15k TPS/card).

- Using 15k TPS/card => steady 160k TPS implies ~11 cards (160 / 15 ≈ 10.7). So Monica's 10-card pick is close; I recommend 11 guaranteed cards to provide headroom for degradation and p99 targets.

- Burst handling: implement a separate burst pool (4 cards) that can be pre-warmed and kept cold when not used. For a 600 QPS sustained spike (~3.2x steady), we need ~200–250k extra TPS for the duration. Four L40S burst cards at cold start won't fully cover, so burst must be allowed to auto-scale or be partially guaranteed. Recommend burst credits equal to ~50% of burst capacity for safety (i.e., ability to spin additional capacity on short notice).

- Memory/long-context: increase KV cache allocation per replica, and reserve some GPU memory for >12k token sessions. This reduces effective TPS/card by ~10% for sessions that use the long contexts — baked into the 15k estimate.

- Latency: p95 streaming should be sub-300ms for small contexts with batching; p99 may be 700–900ms under mixed load unless we increase guaranteed cards. If they need hard p99 SLA <500ms at peak, we should increase guaranteed cards to 13–14.

Recommendation:
- Guaranteed pool: 11 L40S-equivalent cards (targets steady + headroom)
- Burst pool: 4 hot cards + autoscale buffer (on-demand) for campaign spikes
- Commit: 12 months, 30% discount starting point; negotiate to 25% if they want more burst credits as part of package.

If they press for 25% we can add a phased scale plan (start 11 + 2 burst, after 3 months evaluate).

Karthik

Subject: Proposal: Dedicated pool recommendation & commercial path (Velara Tech)

Hi Evan —

Thanks for the telemetry and patience. Attached is a formal recommendation + commercial proposal (Velara_Dedicated_Proposal_20270622.pdf). Executive summary below:

1) Recommended configuration (hybrid):
   - Guaranteed pool: 11 L40S-equivalent GPUs (sized for mixed-context steady-state, ~160k TPS effective).
   - Burst pool: 4 hot GPUs + autoscale-on-demand for additional spikes. Burst credits available for campaign windows (configurable per month).
   - KV/cache: tuned per-replica to support up to 32k contexts (long-context sessions will have reduced batch efficiency; accounted for in sizing).

2) SLA and latency expectations:
   - Steady-state p95 latency (single-shot): ~200–320 ms depending on model and batching mix.
   - Peak p99 with burst engaged: ~600–900 ms. If you require p99 <500 ms at peak, recommend increasing guaranteed cards to 13–14.

3) Commercials & packaging:
   - 12-mo reserved commit (monthly invoiced) for the guaranteed pool.
   - Proposed discount: 30% off hosted on-demand list for the guaranteed GPUs.
   - Burst pool billed at a blended hourly rate; we can include a bucket of burst credits (e.g., 200 GPU-hours/month) as part of the commit.
   - Option: phased ramp (start 11 guaranteed + 2 burst; evaluate after 90 days and scale).

4) Next steps:
   - If this looks good, I'll send the formal MSA/Order Form and a DocuSign link.
   - If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min runbook session with Karthik to walk through autoscale behavior and failover policies.

Attached: Velara_Dedicated_Proposal_20270622.pdf, Velara_MAP.csv (pricing details).

Best,
Monica Patel
